claims.text: The target metallic components have localized surface defects.
The target components are microstructurally sensitive to high thermal input.
Cold spray deposits the repair alloy through a solid-state process without melting it.
Cold spray can create a dense coating on the damaged component.
The cold-sprayed coating will be well adhered to the substrate.
Mechanical interlocking contributes to bonding between the coating and substrate.
The cold-sprayed coating minimizes surface and interfacial defects.
Avoiding melting during deposition prevents thermally induced microstructural degradation.
Avoiding melting during deposition reduces hot cracking relative to traditional fusion-welding repair.
The deposited coating forms a protective barrier against corrosive attack.
The deposited coating protects the substrate against abrasive wear.
Cold-sprayed repairs will have significantly greater hardness than both fusion-welded repairs and untreated damaged surfaces.
Cold-sprayed repairs will have significantly greater wear resistance than both fusion-welded repairs and untreated damaged surfaces.
Cold-sprayed repairs will have significantly greater corrosion resistance than both fusion-welded repairs and untreated damaged surfaces.
Cold-sprayed repairs will exhibit a lower incidence of hot cracking than traditional fusion-welded repairs.
Optional post-treatment below the alloy melting point can enhance coating bonding.
The proposed repair is applicable under aggressive service conditions involving humidity, corrosive media, abrasive loading, or cyclic loading.
